pr_comments: CI: https://ci.nodejs.org/job/node-test-pull-request/35095/

This will likely render the cache significantly less useful. Folders and files are AFAIK also handled separately and this only saves one of them in the cache?
We should validate the cache hit ratio during the loading of a regular project (with lots of modules).

It's implemented like this for a long time and it could be considered a breaking change. Thus, we should carefully evaluate to change this.

> It's implemented like this for a long time and it could be considered a breaking change. Thus, we should carefully evaluate to change this.

If this change doesn't land, a test should be added for the current behavior to make it clear that this is the desired behavior.

And if this change doesn't land, maybe this needs some documenting? [The initial reporter](https://github.com/nodejs/help/issues/3144) was surprised that the documented cache cannot be cleaned via API in this case.

> [The initial reporter](https://github.com/nodejs/help/issues/3144) was surprised that the documented cache cannot be cleaned via API in this case.

There is no real cleaning to do, the `statCache` is temporary and only exists for the duration of an original/root level `require()`.
I'm also -1 on this for the performance reasons and because it seems like a minor edge case.

> I'm also -1 on this for the performance reasons and because it seems like a minor edge case.

But AFAIK, it seems that the benchmark result didn't show any regression on performance. 
https://ci.nodejs.org/view/Node.js%20benchmark/job/benchmark-node-micro-benchmarks/817/
I'm +1 on this if there's no measurable performance difference, but I would like one or more modules folks to review. @nodejs/modules

> But AFAIK, it seems that the benchmark result didn't show any regression on performance.

The current benchmarks don't measure the code being changed here.

The only change here is we didn't set the `statCache` when the result of `internalModuleStat(filename)` less than 0, which usually means there was an error(maybe `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` or something). And I think this was always an edge case, most of time we throw error directly in this case right ?

The most normal scene(we can require module successfully) still cached if the result of `internalModuleStat(filename)` >= 0, so I don't think there would be some performance regression.

How do you think ? 
/cc @mscdex @BridgeAR @nodejs/modules
This seems fine to me.

The determinism/cache only *must* populate on success for `import()` per https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostimportmoduledynamically , I think ejecting prior to any user code/side effects/partial eval seems fine. Reading https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#fetch-a-single-module-script the actual impact of failed network seems a bit complex and only ejects the failed requests keeping successful responses. It never links if there is an ejection though. That behavior seems fine since even with a cycle you can never get to an orphaned source text.

issue_context.title: fs, cjs modules: failed require prevents valid require from loading a module just written by writeFileSync
comments: It's not a race condition. All sync require calls use a single cache that's invalidated afterwards. Thus, as soon as there's anything async, the file is possible to be found.
Maybe require should not be cached on failure

review_comments:
> Folders and files are AFAIK also handled separately and this only saves one of them in the cache?

Folders and files are both handled now. /cc @BridgeAR
